questions.prompt: A Style on `CustomControl` has `<Trigger Property="IsHighlighted" Value="True">` that sets the Background to Yellow. Why does this work without any C# event code?
options: The Style re-reads every property of the control on a short timer
`IsHighlighted` is a dependency property, and WPF listens to its changes
The CLR wrapper's setter raises `PropertyChanged`, which the trigger handles
Triggers only work on properties that were declared in XAML
questions.explanation: `IsHighlighted` is registered with the WPF property system, so the engine listens to the DP and applies the trigger's setters as soon as the value becomes `True`, with no extra C# code.

questions.prompt: What does a class need in order to define its own dependency property?
options: Implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` and back the property with a private field
Be a ViewModel class that is registered in the DI container
Register it with `DependencyProperty.Register` in a `DependencyObject` class
Mark the property with a `[Dependency]` attribute so WPF can find it
questions.explanation: Dependency properties require registration via `DependencyProperty.Register`, and the class must inherit from `DependencyObject`; the CLR wrapper then calls `GetValue`/`SetValue`.

questions.prompt: Which statement about change notification is correct?
options: Both CLR and dependency properties notify the UI automatically
DPs need `INotifyPropertyChanged`, while CLR properties notify automatically
Neither can notify the UI; bindings poll the source for changes instead
CLR properties need `INotifyPropertyChanged`; DPs have built-in notification
questions.explanation: CLR properties do not notify changes automatically, so `INotifyPropertyChanged` is required for binding updates, while dependency properties have built-in change notification and can register callbacks.

questions.prompt: Following the lesson's rule of thumb, how should you implement a `UserName` on `LoginViewModel` and a bindable `SelectedIndex` on a custom dropdown control?
options: `UserName`: CLR property + `INotifyPropertyChanged`; `SelectedIndex`: dependency property
`UserName`: dependency property; `SelectedIndex`: CLR property + `INotifyPropertyChanged`
Both as dependency properties, so both can be bound
Both as plain CLR properties with no notification
questions.explanation: ViewModels (data) use CLR properties with `INotifyPropertyChanged`, which keeps them testable and free of WPF dependencies; controls (UI) use dependency properties for anything that must receive a value from a binding.

source.section: Use CLR Properties for your ViewModels and data models, and Dependency Properties (DP) for Custom Controls and UI elements.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between `TextBox.Text` and `TextBox.TextProperty`?
options: They are two separate values that WPF keeps in sync after each change
`TextProperty` is a CLR wrapper around the `Text` dependency property
`Text` is the CLR wrapper over the static `TextProperty` DP identifier
`Text` is used only in C#, and `TextProperty` only in XAML attributes
questions.explanation: `TextBox.Text` is the instance-level CLR property, and it delegates to the registered `TextBox.TextProperty` dependency property. In XAML you bind with the CLR name (`Text="{Binding ...}"`), but the mechanism relies on `TextProperty`.

questions.prompt: In `PasswordBoxHelper`, the `PasswordChanged` handler sets an internal `IsUpdating` flag to `true` before writing `SecurePassword` and back to `false` afterwards. Why?
options: To make the PasswordBox read-only for as long as the user types
To stop the change being pushed back into the box (a recursive update)
To tell the ViewModel that the new password passed validation
To switch the binding to `UpdateSourceTrigger=LostFocus` for a moment
questions.explanation: `IsUpdating` is an internal marker to prevent recursive updates; `OnSecurePasswordChanged` only updates the PasswordBox when `!GetIsUpdating(passwordBox)`, so a change that came from the user is not written back into the box.

source.section: Secured password Binding using Dependency property
